summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Lynx Medical through the Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards; focused on per-route cost breakdown, token-level cost attribution, and routing fallbacks. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated; security and VPC/KMS concerns were raised. Agreed next steps: send pricing + cost spreadsheet, share technical docs, schedule pilot kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes on the calendar. I'm Samira, AE for Redwood, and with me is Daniel, our SE. Quick intro from your side?
[00:00:12] Dr. Marta Ruiz (Lynx CTO): Hi Samira, Marta here. Eli and Nina on the line too, Tommy is joining—hey.
[00:00:20] Eli Park (Lynx): Hey all.
[00:00:22] Daniel (Redwood SE): Great, we'll start with a short agenda, then go into the console and the per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and then cost breakdowns and Q&A.
[00:00:35] Samira: Quick note, we'll drop links to the deck and the cost spreadsheet in the chat, but we'll also export the console views after.
[00:00:44] Dr. Marta: Sounds good. We're trying to get a feel for unit economics and whether we should go hosted or dedicated for inference. Also security items—Nina will ask those.
[00:00:55] Nina Gomez (Lynx): Yep, SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC are must-haves.
[00:01:05] Samira: Totally, we'll cover those.
[00:01:10] [00:01:10] Daniel: Alright, jumping into the console — I'm screen sharing now, can everyone see my screen?
[00:01:17] Dr. Marta: Yeah we can.
[00:01:20] Daniel: Great. Top nav, usage -> analytics. This page surfaces token consumption, latency P95, and cost per route. We have filters for time range, model, and route tags — so you can slice by product feature, environment, or team.
[00:01:36] Samira: Note that route tags are configurable via our API so you can map routes to product owners, which helps chargeback.
[00:01:44] Eli: How do you attribute embeddings cost vs generation cost if they're shared across routes?
[00:01:50] Daniel: Good question. We do attribution at request-level: each request has a route id, model id, and operation type. If an embedding call is invoked by multiple routes we attribute to the route that made the API call; if you have middleware that fan-outs we'll show the parent/child attribution. It's not perfect if you proxy things, but we can add custom tags.
[00:02:10] [00:02:10] Daniel: Now per-route dashboard — clicking into the 'patient-summarization' route that you saw in the quickstart. You get a breakdown: tokens in, tokens out, model version, average latency, and cost per thousand tokens. There's a cost column that uses your pricing profile and the model's cost profile.
[00:02:30] Eli: Where does the "model cost profile" come from? Is that Redwood's list or our negotiated price?
[00:02:36] Daniel: It's a combination — for hosted it's Redwood's published unit costs, and for dedicated we can plug in your reserved capacity cost model. During pilot we'll configure the pricing profile to reflect your committed nodes.
[00:02:48] Nina: For Private / VPC deployments, do you still show per-route cost? We need on-premise accounting.
[00:02:55] Daniel: Yes, the console supports Private deployments; we can ingest cost signals from your infra (tags on VMs, GPU hours) or you can upload a cost mapping CSV. We often do a one-time mapping during onboarding.
[00:03:08] [00:03:08] Samira: One thing customers like is the token-level cost explorer — you can search a sample of requests and see which prompts are driving up tokens. Useful to optimize prompts and save cost.
[00:03:18] Dr. Marta: Can you demo that?
[00:03:21] Daniel: Sure. Here I'm filtering by route and showing top requests by cost. See this cluster of long prompts — they're coming from a debug mode in our UI. You can also add a threshold alert, e.g., if route cost spikes >20% week-over-week.
[00:03:36] Eli: Does the explorer show KV cache hits or prefix cache hits so we can understand reuse?
[00:03:41] Daniel: We surface cache hit/miss ratios per model and per route, and also show estimated saved tokens. The accuracy depends on whether you enable prefix caching in the runtime.
[00:03:52] [00:03:52] Nina: For compliance, how long are logs retained? We need 12 months of request logs for audit.
[00:03:59] Samira: For hosted, retention is configurable — default 90 days, enterprise add-on for 12/24 months. For Private, retention is whatever you configure in your storage. We'll include retention options in the security docs.
[00:04:14] Dr. Marta: On latency vs cost, we saw your benchmarks showing countertop P95 numbers. If we compress more by quantization or batching, what's the visibility into quality regressions?
[00:04:27] Daniel: Good call. In the console's Optimize module we link per-route evals — you can run small evaluation suites against golden examples and see quality delta when you change quantization profiles. We attach regression alerts to these eval sets.
[00:04:41] [00:04:41] Daniel: For batching, the runtime automatically chooses batching based on latency SLOs. In the console you can set target latency SLO per route; the system will prefer batching for throughput routes and lower batch sizes for latency-critical routes.
[00:04:55] Eli: If we set a global batching policy, can we override per-route?
[00:04:58] Daniel: Yes — policy hierarchy: global -> deployment -> route. Route wins.
[00:05:04] [00:05:04] Samira: Quick qualification — what's your traffic profile? Avg QPS, typical prompt lengths, and expected growth?
[00:05:12] Dr. Marta: Right now we're prototype: 2-4 QPS peak per route, a few routes at 10-15 QPS during batch processing. Prompts average 150 tokens in, 200 tokens out. We expect 3x growth in 6 months if the pilot goes well.
[00:05:28] Eli: Also latency SLOs for patient-facing features need P95 < 600 ms.
[00:05:33] Samira: Good to know. With those numbers dedicated could make sense if you want consistent latency.
[00:05:38] [00:05:38] Daniel: Going back to cost — here's the per-route cost heatmap. Each row is a route, columns are daily cost. Hover shows tokens, model used, and estimated cost. You can export to CSV and we also provide a raw per-request export for billing reconciliation.
[00:05:56] Dr. Marta: How do you handle fallbacks if a model variant is unavailable? For example we want a lower-cost fallback during peak.
[00:06:03] Daniel: Smart routing — you can configure routing policies: prefer low-cost model unless P95 > X, or route by region/capacity. We support automatic fallback to compatible model variants and also multi-tier routing: hosted primary, dedicated fallback, or vice versa.
[00:06:20] [00:06:20] Nina: KMS: do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[00:06:24] Samira: We support KMS in hosted for enterprise: you can bring your keys via customer-managed KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSMs for Private). For full BYOK on hosted we have a documented flow.
[00:06:36] Nina: And audit logs are immutable?
[00:06:39] Daniel: We append logs to write-once storage and sign them; for hosted we provide tamper-evident logs on enterprise plans.
[00:06:47] [00:06:47] Eli: On the cost spreadsheet — will it show per-token cost broken down by input vs output tokens and model weights?
[00:06:54] Daniel: It breaks down input tokens vs output tokens and multiplies by model unit cost. We also show amortized model hot-cache footprint for dedicated nodes so you can see effective cost per token after overhead.
[00:07:06] Dr. Marta: For dedicated, what's the expected uplift for 95th percentile throughput? I mean how much headroom do we reserve?
[00:07:14] Samira: That depends on your commitment. We typically size for steady-state QPS with a small burst headroom. We'll recommend configs after we see more traffic patterns from pilot benchmarks.
[00:07:24] [00:07:24] Daniel: Quick demo of alerts: here is a per-route cost anomaly alert rule tied to billing; when cost increases >20% and token length distribution shifts, it creates a ticket in Sentry or your webhook.
[00:07:36] Eli: Is there an API for exporting usage for our internal billing?
[00:07:39] Daniel: Yes, we have a usage export API (CSV/JSON). You can request a daily or hourly feed with per-request metadata including route id, tokens, model, and cost attribution.
[00:07:50] [00:07:50] Nina: What about SSO and RBAC? We need scoped API keys and role-based access for different teams.
[00:07:56] Samira: SSO (SAML/OIDC) is standard; RBAC with custom roles is on enterprise plans. Scoped API keys and token scoping is supported so you can limit by route/role.
[00:08:07] Daniel: Also, the console has a policy simulator so you can preview least-privilege roles.
[00:08:14] [00:08:14] Dr. Marta: Ok let's talk pilot. We're interested in a 6-week pilot on hosted with a follow-up to evaluate dedicated. What would you need from us?
[00:08:23] Samira: We'll need a small set of routes (3-5) to instrument, sample traffic or replay logs, access to a sandbox project, and SSO/SCIM to provision. We'll run benchmarks and share the cost spreadsheet.
[00:08:34] Eli: For the benchmark, what do you measure exactly?
[00:08:37] Daniel: Latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, KV cache hit rates, cost per 1k tokens, and quality evaluation against golden examples. We'll also run a small stress test for autoscaling and tail latency.
[00:08:50] [00:08:50] Samira: I'm going to pause for questions.
[00:08:53] Dr. Marta: Two quick ones: can we restrict data residency to eu-west for some routes?
[00:08:58] Daniel: Yes, routing by region is supported; you can pin routes to a region or deployment to ensure residency.
[00:09:05] Nina: Are there guarantees around egress to third parties? We need to ensure no third-party access to unencrypted payloads.
[00:09:12] Samira: Redwood never shares customer payloads; hosted enterprise offers encryption-at-rest and in-transit and we support private tenancy for extra isolation. We'll send the security packet.
[00:09:22] [00:09:22] Daniel: Back to console, here's the per-route trend: you can group routes into buckets 'patient-facing', 'internal', etc., and see aggregated cost. Also, you can run hypothetical what-if scenarios — e.g., switch model X to quantized variant and estimate cost/latency change.
[00:09:40] Eli: That what-if estimator — how accurate is it?
[00:09:44] Daniel: It's an estimate based on model performance profiles and your route's token distribution. We include margins. For final sizing we recommend real benchmarks.
[00:09:54] [00:09:54] Samira: We're about 10 minutes in, we're conscious of time—want to make sure we cover action items.
[00:10:00] Dr. Marta: Could you show an example CSV export?
[00:10:03] Daniel: Sure — exporting now. The CSV includes timestamp, request id, route id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, cache_hit, and tags.
[00:10:14] Nina: Will that include trove-level PII? We need to redact or limit fields for audit copies.
[00:10:20] Daniel: You can toggle PII redaction for exports; for hosted enterprise we provide redaction profiles.
[00:10:28] [00:10:28] Eli: A practical question: If we move to dedicated later, will we lose historical hosted analytics?
[00:10:34] Samira: No, analytics persist in the control plane and you can combine historical hosted and dedicated data for continuous dashboards.
[00:10:42] [00:10:42] Dr. Marta: On pricing — do you bill per-token on hosted only, or is there a hybrid for dedicated?
[00:10:49] Samira: For hosted it's per-token/on-demand. For dedicated it's committed capacity (node-month) plus a small per-token overage. We can model both in the spreadsheet so you can compare TCO given your traffic profile.
[00:11:03] [00:11:03] Daniel: Quick note on autoscaling — dedicated pools can autoscale based on queue length and CPU/GPU utilization; you can configure burst capacity to avoid throttles.
[00:11:13] Eli: Any SLAs for P95 latencies?
[00:11:16] Samira: Enterprise SLAs cover availability and we offer latency targets for dedicated deployments; we'll include proposed SLA language in the contract draft.
[00:11:26] [00:11:26] Nina: Security question — do you do pentests and provide reports?
[00:11:30] Daniel: Yes, Redwood runs regular penetration tests; we can provide summaries and SOC2 report under NDA.
[00:11:38] [00:11:38] Samira: We're wrapping up—recap of next steps: I'll send the pricing deck and per-route cost spreadsheet, Daniel will share the benchmarking guide and KB on caching, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff with your infra team for week of 10/11.
[00:11:53] Dr. Marta: Great. One more ask — can you include an example of a per-route SLA we can show our procurement folks?
[00:11:59] Samira: Yes, we'll include sample SLA language in the packet.
[00:12:05] [00:12:05] Eli: Thanks both.
[00:12:07] Nina: Thanks.
[00:12:09] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email.
[00:12:14] [End of recorded portion — remaining time used for brief side conversations between AE/SE and customer offline]

Note: transcription has typical minor errors (names, acronyms) and occasional timestamps misaligned due to auto-generation.
